ai_show_review.summary: High‑octane China>Rider>High Time jam and relentless Lovelight sequence
ai_show_review.blurb: The show rockets through a scorching China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time stretch, then rolls into an unstoppable Not Fade Away → Drums → Good Lovin' → The Other One → Turn On Your Lovelight cycle. Jerry’s voice is emotional on Black Peter while the rhythm section drives a machine‑gun groove. Pigpen’s vocal power shines especially during the Lovelight finale.
ai_show_review.review: On March 7, 1970 at the Santa Monica Civic Auditorium the Dead delivered a blistering one‑set performance that still thrills listeners despite the tape’s fair audience quality. The highlight is undoubtedly the seamless China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time sequence – Jerry’s guitar burns, Bob matches him note for note and the crowd rides the high‑octane wave straight into a ferocious Not Fade Away that morphs into an extended drum jam. From there the band launches into Good Lovin’, The Other One and a second Not Fade Away that funnels into a monster Turn On Your Lovelight, with Pigpen’s soulful vocals cutting through Mickey and Bill’s tribal percussion. Black Peter showcases a surprisingly pretty, emotional vocal from Jerry, while Phil’s bass provides a relentless machine‑gun pulse throughout the set. Though the audience recording carries hiss, crackles and occasional drop‑outs, it captures the raw energy and tight interplay that make this night a must‑listen for any 1970 era fan.

best_recording.reason: Only complete recording of the show; despite fair audience quality it preserves the high‑energy performance and key jams.

key_highlights: Scorching China Cat Sunflower → I Know You Rider → High Time jam
Relentless Not Fade Away → Drums → Good Lovin' → The Other One → Turn On Your Lovelight sequence
Pigpen’s vocal power on Turn On Your Lovelight and throughout the set
Mickey and Bill’s tribal drum break that drives the second half

band_performance.Jerry: His voice is pretty and emotional on Black Peter; guitar work is fast, furious and burning during the China → Rider stretch and The Other One.
band_performance.Phil: Bass lines are a ‘machine‑gun’ intensity that drives Good Lovin' and powers the NFA/Drums groove.
band_performance.Bob: Delivers burning rhythm guitar that lights up the road especially in the China → Rider segment.
band_performance.Pigpen: Vocal power shines throughout; strong showmanship on Turn On Your Lovelight, adding soulful grit to the climax.
band_performance.Mickey: Stomps like a tribe; drum break considered ‘ON’ and propels the extended jam sections.
band_performance.Billy: Pairs with Mickey in tribal, stomping drumming that fuels the high‑energy flow of the set.
